question: The Sikhs under Guru Hargobind defeated the Mughals four times during the reign of ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Guru Hargobind was the sixth Sikh Guru and led the Sikh community in battles against the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Sikhs, under Guru Hargobind, defeated the Mughals four times during the reign of Shah Jahan.
 
• The battles were significant as they established the martial tradition within Sikhism, emphasizing the need for Sikhs to defend their faith and community.
 
• Guru Hargobind introduced the concept of Miri and Piri, representing temporal and spiritual authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Hargobind:**

 
 
• He was the sixth of the ten Sikh Gurus and became Guru on 25 May 1606, following the martyrdom of his father, Guru Arjan.
 
• He constructed the Akal Takht, which stands in the Harmandir Sahib complex, as a symbol of political sovereignty and justice.
 
 
 
• **Mughal-Sikh Conflicts:**
 
 
• The battles between the Mughals and Sikhs were mainly due to the growing power and influence of the Sikh community.
 
• These conflicts were part of a larger series of confrontations between the Mughal Empire and various regional powers and communities.
 
 
 
• **Miri and Piri:**
 
 
• This concept introduced by Guru Hargobind denotes the dual responsibility of the Sikh community to lead a spiritual life while also taking up arms to defend justice.
 
• Miri represents temporal authority, while Piri signifies spiritual authority.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1628 to 1658.
 
• He is best known for commissioning the Taj Mahal, a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
